# Keytab fixtures

## `mit-multi-enctype.keytab`

- **Source:** disposable MIT FILE keytab generated by the hermetic Go test
  harness.
- **MIT version:** Ubuntu MIT krb5 `1.19.2-2ubuntu0.8`.
- **Command:** `./integration/fixtures/generate.sh` (which runs
  `go test -tags integration ./integration/mit -run '^TestGenerateFixtures$'
  -count=1 -v`); the harness executes `kadmin.local -q 'addprinc
  -randkey host/service.test'` followed by `kadmin.local -q 'ktadd -k
  services.keytab -e aes128-cts-hmac-sha1-96,aes256-cts-hmac-sha1-96,
  aes128-cts-hmac-sha256-128,aes256-cts-hmac-sha384-192 host/service.test'`.
- **Realm:** `TEST.GOKRB5.LOCAL`.
- **Principal:** `host/service.test@TEST.GOKRB5.LOCAL`.
- **Enctypes:** AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 (17), AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 (18),
  AES128-CTS-HMAC-SHA256-128 (19), and AES256-CTS-HMAC-SHA384-192 (20).
- **Interpretation:** four MIT FILE keytab v2 entries for one service
  principal; KVNO and enctype are visible with `klist -k -e`. The key bytes
  are synthetic and are not logged or otherwise used as credentials.

The realm, database, keytab, and all configuration files are created below
`testing.T.TempDir()` and are removed during test cleanup.
